On Wed, Mar 13, 2029 at 10:58 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben / Marissa / Jonas — looping you in. Sam reported transient 503s and elevated p50/p95 for Clearline's reserved pool starting ~07:30 UTC. Preliminary checks: autoscaler did a brief scale-up, but we observed a provisioning backlog on a subset of hot nodes for ~4 minutes. No driver crashes.

I pulled the allocator trace and node-init logs. Summary: two nodes experienced delayed image pull due to a registry rate-limiter interaction with our staging mirror. Node readiness delayed by ~220s on those nodes which created short-lived queue pressure; autoscaler then throttled additional launches for ~3m while the controller reconciled available capacity. The fallback routing attempted to spill to warm standby but one routing rule (tenant shuffling policy v2) evaluated incorrectly and kept a small fraction of traffic pinned to the delayed nodes for ~30s. Total customer-impact window ~3:50.

I've attached the health snapshot and the minimal routing diff I used to validate the condition. Root cause appears to be the mirror rate limit combined with a brittle tenant-shuffle predicate under mid-scale events.

Attachment: pool-health-snapshot-2029-03-13.csv (csv); routing-policy-diff-2029-03-13.txt (text)

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sam.ortiz@clearline.ai
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 12:07:30 -07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent timeouts this morning on dedicated pool

Sam — thanks for flagging and for the log snippet. Quick update on what we know and next steps: 

What happened (short):
- A subset of new nodes for your reserved pool experienced delayed startup because our staging mirror hit a transient rate limit when pulling an image.
- The autoscaler initiated scale-up, but two nodes were late to join the pool which caused queuing and a small number of 503s.
- A tenant-shuffle rule mis-evaluated and kept ~5% of traffic targeted at the affected nodes for 30s longer than ideal.

Impact window: ~07:30–07:34 UTC (we estimate ~3–4 minutes of intermittent elevated latency and a handful of 503s).

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Disabled the failing tenant-shuffle predicate and enforced strict fallback-to-standby for affected subpools.
- Added an emergency bypass on image pulls that routes to the primary registry to avoid the mirror until we harden rate-limit handling.

Actions we're taking (next 48 hours):
- Complete a post-incident evidence packet with allocator traces, routing evaluation logs, and node-init timing (deliverable by 2029-03-14 18:00 UTC).
- Patch: make the tenant-shuffle policy resilient to partial node readiness (targeted rollout by 2029-03-15).
- Preventative: add backpressure detection for mirror pulls and a fast-fail fallback to primary registry (ETA 2029-03-20).

Customer ask: can you confirm whether you saw any user-facing error rates or material business impact beyond the trace you sent? We want to make sure the credit / remediation conversation has accurate scope.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@clearline.ai>

Thanks — that all makes sense and appreciate the clear next steps. We saw increased retries in our telemetry and a small spike in user-facing errors for ~4 minutes; nothing that triggered alerts on our side beyond higher latency counts. Clearing a couple follow-ups from our end:

- Procurement asked if you could include the evidence packet in a form we can attach to an internal SLA incident (PDF or shared Drive link).
- We're ok with the proposed mitigations but would like an ETA on the tenant-shuffle policy patch and confirmation when the registry fallback is live.

If you can send the evidence packet and a short one-paragraph summary we can attach to our internal postmortem, that would be helpful. Appreciate your team's responsiveness.

— Sam
